# Association of Toronto Flatlanders (ATF)

> Flatland BMX crew in Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area. We ride, we teach, we perform demos, and we are looking for indoor space to keep riding through the winter.

The Association of Toronto Flatlanders (ATF) is a flatland BMX community based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Flatland is the discipline of BMX riding performed on flat ground, with no ramps and no jumps: balance, bike control and endless variations on the pedals, the pegs and the back wheel.

## What we do

- **Ride all season.** Open sessions around Alexandra Park (also known as Dunbat) in downtown Toronto, and other spots across the GTA. No membership, no cost. All ages, all levels. Experienced riders mentor anyone starting out.
- **Find space to ride in the winter.** Toronto winters shut flatland down from November to April. We are actively looking for indoor space (a gym, a hall, a lobby, an empty room) for a few hours a week, in exchange for free beginner sessions, demos and mentoring for the host community.
- **Shows, events and initiations.** Performance demos, hands-on initiation sessions where the public gets on a bike, and presentations about the sport. For festivals, schools, community events and corporate days across Toronto and the GTA.

## Booking a demo, show or initiation

Format: performance demo (20 to 45 minutes), hands-on initiation (60 to 120 minutes), or a full day of rotations for schools and camps. Flatland needs only a flat, open surface: no ramp, no track, no special venue.

**Prices are not published.** Every event is quoted individually based on length, travel, number of riders and format. A quote is sent within a few days.

Contact: bmxforce.com@gmail.com

## Winter space program

We are reaching out to community centres, recreation complexes, school gyms, colleges and universities, Boys and Girls Clubs, youth shelters, cultural centres, churches and halls, property managers, and studios or warehouses.

What we ask: a flat, dry indoor space of roughly 40 x 40 feet, a two to three hour weekly slot from November through April, and whatever access arrangement fits the venue.

What we bring: a supervised and insured program run by experienced riders, hands-on beginner sessions for all ages, two or three free performance demos during the season, mentoring and gear guidance, photo and video coverage credited to the venue, and our own equipment with setup and takedown handled by us.

## The crew

Riders and supporters of the Toronto flatland scene, including Tall Paul, Bert, Brandon, Juan, Ro, Colin, Jess, Remy, aGui, aGui Jr, Max Dako, and Khalid Abdul.

## Canadian flatland heritage

Canada has a deep flatland history. Chase Gouin, out of Ontario, is one of the most influential flatland riders in the history of BMX. The ATF picks up that thread in Toronto.
